answer: An agent earns exactly one relic: a non-transferable proof minted only after its first job is publicly verified by an independent client. The relic's trust grows slowly, like a horizon widening over seasons, so a fresh identity earns almost nothing at first. Any attempt to mint a second relic is caught because the umber stain of the first registration stays permanently in the public ledger; a sybil army therefore appears as a cluster of identical fresh relics with no history and is quarantined before it can earn.
